summary.headline: Pyramid Technoplast Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to ₹222 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 10% and capacity utilisation only 62%.
summary.overview:
Revenue grew 36% YoY to ₹222 crore, driven mainly by price pass-through of raw material increases, while volumes were 1,292 MT against 20,936 MT per quarter installed capacity (about 62% utilisation). Gross margin compressed to 23% and EBITDA grew 50% YoY at about 10% margin; PAT rose 32% YoY to ₹10.5 crore at about 5% margin. Management said EBITDA per ton was ₹16,380 versus ₹11,252 a year earlier and ₹15,053 in Q4 FY26, but also said the figure reflects a temporary price spike that is expected to normalise. Management announced a ₹20-25 crore Kutch (IBC) plant due by March 2027 and government subsidy approvals of about ₹24.9 crore (WADA) and ₹10.5 crore (Bharuch unit 7) over 10 years.</overview>

segments.name: HDPE drums
segments.commentary: Tonnage down 4% YoY; management said gross margin in rupee terms for HDPE remained stable.

segments.name: IBC
segments.commentary: Volumes hit as export demand suffered from Middle East disruption and higher freight costs; management said exports were only 2-4% of mix.

segments.name: MS drums
segments.commentary: Strong growth cited, partly offsetting HDPE and IBC weakness; no figure given.

segments.name: WADA unit
segments.commentary: Running above 70% utilisation, targeted at 80% this year; contributed ~₹43 crore (~19% of revenue) in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 targets: ~15% revenue growth and EBITDA margin above 10%; in Q&A management said 11-12% and that FY27 EBITDA could reach ₹85-86 crore, versus an earlier ₹80 crore figure.
Polymer drum selling price expected to fall about ₹20 (from ~₹160 to ~₹140) over 3-6 months, with management saying margin would rise to 11% once prices normalise.
Overall utilisation expected at 70-75% by year-end (Q&A), versus 80% previously cited; WADA targeted at 80%.
Kutch IBC plant (10,000 IBC/month, ₹20-25 crore) expected by March 2027; initial revenue assumed ₹50 crore, with commercial production from FY28 and payback in about 4 years.
FY27 capex ~₹20-25 crore, mainly Kutch; WADA phase 2 (~₹20-25 crore, ~₹400 crore revenue potential) planned after March 2027.
Solar: 1 MW pending, expected to be commissioned next quarter; management said FY27 solar savings would be below ₹15 crore, with full run-rate later.
Subsidy: management said ~₹3.5 crore per year over 10 years, with timing of receipt in FY27 uncertain.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 20,936 MT per quarter; utilisation ~62% in Q1 FY27.
WADA unit operating above 70% utilisation; management said it has added capacity and is not allowed to add more until after March due to subsidy terms.
Kutch: ₹20-25 crore for a 10,000 IBC/month facility on owned land, ~₹10 crore for land and building; expected commissioning by March 2027, production start in about 8 months.
Solar: 6 MW (Oct 2025), 5 MW Bharuch, 2.25 MW Maharashtra; 1 MW pending. Recycling plant (5,000 MT/yr, commissioned Oct 2025) addresses 10-12% of raw material needs.
PUC/environmental licence: 90% of work done, one licence pending; partial capacity can run in the meantime.
demand_pricing: Polymer drum selling price about ₹160/kg in Q1 FY27 versus ₹138 in March per an analyst's question; management said polymer cost rose from about ₹100 to ₹150 and expects prices to ease.
Management said the Middle East war raised freight costs and cut exports, with exports only about 2-4% of mix but a larger knock-on effect on IBC and drum customers.
Management said raw material is now sourced mainly locally, with imports only when 5-10/kg cheaper; inventory held for about 45 days.
Kutch: management said the market is ~10,000 IBC versus ~2,000 currently served from Bharuch; 30% of benefit to be shared with customers initially.
Debtor days 65-70; working capital rising due to higher raw material prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is steady-state utilisation and the path from 62%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation would reach about 70% this year, with WADA going to 80%; export slowdown due to Middle East freight costs was the main drag.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA per ton of ₹16,380 persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has normalised: selling price of ~₹160 expected to fall to ~₹140, with EBITDA margin rising to 10-11% and a target of 11-12% this year.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 EBITDA reach ₹85-86 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is 'complete hope', without giving a number.

qa_highlights.question: Will solar savings reach ₹15 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹15 crore is the full-year run-rate after all 14.25 MW is commissioned and running; FY27 will be below that, with savings linked to production and solar generation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q1 margin below expectations and why no inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the price gap (~₹40/kg between cost and selling price) compressed margins, and the 45-day inventory gain was booked in March, not Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kutch subsidy cash or GST-linked, and when is it received?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is GST-linked, spread over 10 years (~₹3.5 crore a year), with receipt timing uncertain; Kutch will be funded from internal accruals.
